newsitem.title: USA: Disputes at WTO over agricultural language - USDA's Rominger.
newsitem.headline: Disputes at WTO over agricultural language - USDA's Rominger.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Agriculture Secretary Richard Rominger said by telephone from Singapore on Tuesday that discussion of agricultural trade issues was delayed at the World Trade Organization meeting due to "some disagreement" among nations.

Rominger told reporters that trade leaders might not touch on agriculture until Friday, the final day of the meeting, while efforts were made to iron out differences. He described the dispute as a question of how much emphasis to give freer agricultural trade in the final report on the meeting.
"There is some disagreement" about the language that would go into the declaration, Rominger said in a telephone news conference. "So, we're still working," he said.

"We want to keep the emphasis on agriculture but we also want to come out of this conference with agreement, rather than acrimony," he added, so there would be harmony as nations prepared for a new round to trade negotiations in 1999.
Japan, South Korea and the European Union preferred less emphasis on agriculture while the Cairns Group of free-trading nations, led by Argentina, want a focus on freer agricultural trade.

Rominger said the meeting in Singapore allowed a review of progress in the first two years of GATT to reduce sharply the use of export subsidies and unfair farm subsidies and to press for allegiance to its timetable. He chided Hungary and the Philippines for foot-dragging.
He expects WTO to grow, and foresaw development as well of smaller regional multilateral trade pacts which must be "complementary to the WTO."
Several meetings with other nations, including China, were planned, said Rominger, who already met EU leaders.
